root_idea.summary: The root centers on reporting that something occurs, is present, or comes to be, with reference to past or present time.
root_idea.development: This orientation develops into the existential and copular verb كَانَ and related ideas of being and coming into existence. The derivation of مَكَانٌ from كَانَ يَكُونُ is reported as a qualified view, not as an established direct meaning of the root.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Classical Arabic Form I citation verb.
Displayed as the distinct noun مَكَانَةٌ.
Displayed as the normalized noun مَكَانٌ.
The LOC-tagged occurrences are the same lexical noun مَكَانٌ; the additional tag is syntactic rather than a distinct public lexeme.

senses.definition: To be, exist, or be in a stated condition; also to serve as a copula linking a subject with its predicate.
senses.usage_conditions: It commonly presents a state or existence with past-time reference, but the surrounding construction may yield present, future, habitual, or counterfactual translations. It may be used without an independently emphasized time meaning as a copula. With divine predicates or generic subjects, it can mark a characteristic understood as enduring or little subject to separation; a past reference may describe either a continuing state or one that later changed. In كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ, the past form can point to the status assigned in divine determination or judgment rather than simply replacing a present-tense form.

senses.definition: To occur, come about, or be realized or present.
senses.usage_conditions: Explicitly attested in the conditional construction إِنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ, where the sense is that a hardship or condition has occurred or is present.

senses.definition: A place of being or existence; a place or position occupied by someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun can refer literally to a place, as well as to the place in which a group or thing is situated.

senses.definition: Position, standing, or state; the condition or station in which someone is placed.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially in expressions concerning a person's or group's position, standing, or condition.
Includes a physical location or a designated place; the LOC-tagged Quranic occurrences are included under this same noun.
Used figuratively for a person's or group's position or station, including a place in an evaluative or social order.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In some technical usage, the transformation of a substance into something lower than it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A qualified usage attributed to some speakers; it is not presented as a general Quranic sense of كَانَ.
A theological technical usage attributed to many theologians.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive or take on being; to come into existence or originate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V; describes emergence into existence rather than merely being in a state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become lowly, humble, submissive, or abased.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X; commonly describes humble submission, including submission before or to someone addressed with لِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guarantee or undertake responsibility for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, explicitly qualified usage with عَلَى: كُنْتُ عَلَى فُلَانٍ أَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the command مَكَانَكَ, to stay where one is.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional imperative expression meaning “remain where you are.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ground, basis, or warrant for saying something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction هٰذَا مَكَانٌ لِقَوْلِنَا كَذَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become as or like something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَصْبَحَ مَكَانَ كَذَا, “it became as or like such a thing.”

cautions: The derivation of مَكَانٌ from كَانَ يَكُونُ is reported as a qualified lexical view, not asserted as certain.
كَانَ often functions grammatically as an auxiliary or copula, so English tense choices are strongly dependent on construction and context.
Historical citation notation in the lexical evidence has not been converted into additional modern Quran locations; the examples use only supplied QAC locations.
